QuestionStmt.S: A simple pendulum with bob of mass m and conducting wire of length L swings under gravity through an angle θ. The component of earth's magnetic field in the direction perpendicular to swing is B. Maximum e.m.f. induced across the pendulum is (g = acceleration due to gravity)

Solution.S:
Height from mean position: $h = L - L\cos\theta = 2L\sin^2(\theta/2)$.

Using energy conservation: $\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = mgh \Rightarrow v = 2\sqrt{gL}\sin(\theta/2)$.

Maximum induced emf: $\varepsilon_{\text{max}} = B L v = B L \times 2\sqrt{gL}\sin(\theta/2) = 2BL\sqrt{gL}\sin(\theta/2)$.

Thus the correct option is A.
